compiled_state.title: [code-reviewer-standard]: missing-reference findings without subdirectory search -> hallucinated file-does-not-exist false positives
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** $(git rev-parse HEAD)

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Before emitting any 'file X does not exist' or 'reference Y is unresolved' finding, the reviewer must verify the file is absent across the repository — not just at the literal path the consumer references. The dso shim itself learned subdirectory cascade in PR #173 (bug 0736-a97e) because referenced scripts may live in subdirectories like plugins/dso/scripts/sprint/ rather than plugins/dso/scripts/. The reviewer's MANDATORY pre-check (added by bug ece7-52a1) already requires read_files verification, but does not require subdirectory search.

#### Actual Behavior

PR #197 flagged 'workflow invokes non-existent validation script: validate-required-checks.sh is referenced but does not exist' at IMPORTANT severity. The script existed in plugins/dso/scripts/onboarding/. The reviewer issued the read_files request for the literal path and got 'not found', then emitted the finding without searching subdirectories. This is the same root cause as bug 0736-a97e but reproduced in the reviewer pre-check protocol.

#### Evidence

* PR #197 finding: workflow file referenced \`bash plugins/dso/scripts/onboarding/validate-required-checks.sh\` (correct path) — reviewer flagged it missing because the read_files request resolved at the basename level
* Per-branch-review.yml line 117 cited as the assertion site
* PR analysis: 3 of 27 findings (11%) are hallucinated reference findings = 19% of FPs

### 3. Action History

* Bug ece7-52a1 added the read_files pre-check requirement to code-reviewer-standard.md
* Subdirectory cascade was not part of that fix

### 4. Proposed Fix

Strengthen the MANDATORY pre-check in reviewer-delta-standard.md: before emitting any 'file does not exist' / 'missing reference' finding, require either (a) a \`find . -name <basename>\` request via the grep action with pattern matching, or (b) a recursive grep search over the repo. Only emit the finding if NO match is found anywhere in the repo, not just at the literal cited path. Mirror the dso shim's subdirectory cascade (bug 0736-a97e) at the reviewer-prompt level.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affected agent: code-reviewer-standard
* Affected delta: reviewer-delta-standard.md
* Affected build: build-review-agents.sh
* Research support: docs/findings/code-review-fp-research-2026-05-17.md §9 (proposal B)

### 6. Logs

Estimated effect of fix: kills 50–70% of hallucinated-reference FPs → –6–8% on FP rate.

comments.body: Status update (2026-05-17): initial implementation shipped via PR #212 (merge commit 464ecfebd8). CodeRabbit caught a design defect in §B during the merge review: the prompt instructed reviewers to issue a content 'grep' request for the basename, but 'grep' searches file contents, not filenames — so a basename grep would match every workflow / script / doc that REFERENCES the basename, not the file itself, and would suppress legitimate 'file does not exist' findings (false negatives). The within-contract fix is a multi-path 'read_files' candidate cascade: reviewer constructs the basename under common subdirectory prefixes and the dispatcher reads every candidate in one call. Existence is proven only when ALL candidates return missing. Follow-up shipped as PR #213 (branch fix/code-reviewer-b-design-defect). Will close this ticket when PR #213 merges.
comments.author: Test
